item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A unit of Japan's Daiichi Life (8750.T) has made an indicative proposal to buy more than 79% of shares in Australian investment manager Challenger (CGF.AX) it does not already own, Challenger said on Monday. Shares of the Australian firm jumped over 15% to A$11.33 by 2305 GMT, hitting their highest level since October 23, 2018. Under the proposal, the Japanese insurer is offering A$11.80 apiece, valuing Challenger at A$7.94 billion ($5.53 billion). The offer represents a premium of 19.8% over the stock's closing price on Friday. The unit, TAL Daiichi Life Australia Pty, holds 20.36% of the Australian investment manager, according to LSEG. Daiichi Life, through its unit, had initially acquired a 15.1% minority stake in Challenger from MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings in April 2025 . The takeover proposal is subject to a number of conditions including satisfactory completion of due diligence, Challenger said on Monday. "The Board of Challenger is considering the indicative offer," the Australian firm added. In a separate statement, Daiichi Life confirmed that TAL Daiichi Life Australia has submitted a non-binding proposal to the board of directors of Challenger, adding that no decision has been made by the company on proceeding with the binding transaction. Separately, Challenger reported a 5% rise in its assets under management to $31.9 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, citing strong sales momentum across both domestic and offshore annuities. ($1 = 1.4360 Australian dollars)

item.title: Mbappe double helps Real Madrid sweep aside Sevilla ahead of El Clasico
item.description: Real Madrid closed the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to six points.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to six points with a 4-1 win over Sevilla at the Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday, a week before the rivals meet. Real, who have won three straight games in all competitions following the international break, climbed to third on 21 points, one behind Atletico Madrid, while Sevilla are sixth on 14. Elsewhere, Osasuna withstood second-half pressure from Racing Santander to win 2-0 in Jagoba Arrasate's first game back as manager. Two flying saves from Ionut Radu denied Alaves a point in a 2-1 defeat to Celta Vigo, while Real Sociedad won 5-2 at Malaga. REAL TURN ON THE STYLE Despite the suspended Vinicius Jr's absence, Real produced the fluid attacking football that has been lacking of late with Arda Guler again orchestrating their best work. After a stale opening, the Turkey international sparked the match into life. Sevilla appealed for a red card following an incident involving Guler and Peque Fernandez, but Guler responded minutes later by collecting Yan Diomande's pass and arrowing a shot into the top corner. Mbappe scored an equally impressive second in the 37th minute, turning brilliantly to burst through on goal before calmly beating Odysseas Vlachodimos. Fede Valverde, restored to right back by coach Jose Mourinho, made a crucial block to deny Felix Correia just before the hour as Sevilla threatened to work their way back into the contest. Diomande then exploited the space created by Sevilla’s more adventurous approach, evading his marker before sending Mbappe in behind the defence. Andres Castrin brought down the French forward, who got to his feet to convert the resulting penalty and effectively settle the contest. Substitute Manu Bueno reduced Sevilla’s arrears with a composed finish 10 minutes from time after Mbappe cheaply surrendered possession deep inside his own half. Diomande restored Real's three-goal advantage two minutes later, capping a fine display with a thunderous strike. Eder Militao received a warm ovation when he came on in the 85th minute for his first appearance since undergoing hamstring surgery in April. Mourinho will take encouragement from one of the most complete performances of his second spell at Real as they prepare for next Sunday's pivotal meeting with Barcelona.

item.title: Bryce Young, Panthers control banged-up Eagles
item.description: Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tommy Tremble and the Carolina Panthers' defense was solid in a 25-14 road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tommy Tremble and the Carolina Panthers' defense was solid in a 25-14 road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon. Young finished 20-for-39 for 281 yards. Backfield mate Chuba Hubbard rushed for 120 yards and a touchdown on 28 carries. Ryan Fitzgerald kicked two long field goals to help the Panthers (3-2) to their second road triumph in three tries this year. Tanner McKee threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in his season debut as the Eagles (2-4) lost their fourth consecutive game. McKee, appearing in his seventh career game, filled in for Jalen Hurts, who was placed on injured reserve Saturday after he was diagnosed with a blood clot in his leg last week. The Eagles punted eight times and collected 17 first downs. Fitzgerald's 52-yard field goal on the first possession of the second half marked the only scoring in the third quarter. The Panthers went on a 92-yard drive that concluded with Hubbard's 1-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter. A two-point conversion pass failed, leaving the score at 19-7. The Eagles responded with McKee's 19-yard touchdown throw to DeVonta Smith with 10:42 to play. A blocked Eagles punt gave Carolina favorable field position. The Panthers needed to go just 48 yards for an insurance touchdown, with Young connecting with Tremble on a 19-yard scoring strike with 6:34 left. Carolina went up 10-0 on Young's 12-yard pass to Tremble in the second quarter. Dameon Pierce put the Eagles on the board with a 2-yard run with 2:42 remaining in the first half. Carolina outgained the Eagles 178-110 in the half, which ended at 10-7. The Panthers, fresh off an open week on the schedule, got a 47-yard field goal from Fitzgerald on their first possession. Philadelphia's first two possessions resulted in a net of minus-3 yards. The Eagles punted three times in the first quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Saints build big lead, then need to hold off Giants for win
item.description: Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for a touchdown and the visiting New Orleans Saints held off the New York Giants 34-27 on Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for a touchdown and the visiting New Orleans Saints held off the New York Giants 34-27 on Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford, N.J. The Saints (2-4) ended a three-game losing streak as they rushed for a season-high 175 yards and Martin Emerson Jr. had two of the team's three interceptions. Jameis Winston passed for one touchdown and two interceptions for the Giants (3-2-1) before being replaced by J.J. McCarthy, who led a dramatic late comeback. On the first possession of the second half, Shough threw a short pass to Alvin Kamara, who turned the play into a 31-yard touchdown that gave New Orleans a 17-10 lead. Shough sneaked 1 yard for a touchdown and the Saints' fourth score in as many possessions, pushing the lead to 24-10. Daniel Carlson's 51-yard field goal increased the lead to 27-10 at the end of the third quarter. Julian Blackmon's interception of Winston led to Shough's 18-yard touchdown pass to Chris Olave to expand the lead to 34-10. McCarthy replaced Winston and threw an interception before driving the Giants 45 yards in 2:31 and capping the sequence with a 5-yard touchdown pass to Tyrone Tracy Jr. New York converted a subsequent 2-point conversion and then needed only 48 seconds to score again on McCarthy's 24-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely (with a failed 2-point try). After forcing a Saints 3-and-out, Dominic Zvada's 41-yard field goal trimmed the New Orleans lead to 34-27 with 2:04 left. New York forced another punt and McCarthy, who finished with 243 passing yards, drove the Giants to the Saints 14, but they turned the ball over on downs with five seconds left. Malik Nabers finished with 12 catches for 165 yards for New York. The Giants' second possession was a 12-play, 93-yard drive that ended with Winston's 17-yard touchdown pass to Tracy to give them a 7-0 lead at the end of the first quarter. Zvada's 34-yard field goal early in the second quarter increased the lead to 10-0. Carlson kicked a 58-yard field goal for New Orleans' first points, and on the ensuing kickoff Charlie Jones fumbled and Oscar Delp recovered for the Saints at the New York 28. On fourth-and-goal, Shough threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to Bryce Lance to tie the score 10-10 at halftime. --Field Level Media

item.title: Browns get walk-off winner to catch Ravens in AFC North
item.description: Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cleveland Browns a 13-10 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and a share of first place in the AFC North.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cleveland Browns a 13-10 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and a share of first place in the AFC North. Deshaun Watson connected with Jerry Jeudy on a 33-yard pass to the Baltimore 29-yard line with 22 seconds remaining to set up the decisive kick. Szmyt's initial attempt from 42 yards was blocked by Keyon Martin, who was flagged for offside. Szmyt then drilled his second attempt through the uprights. Carson Schwesinger racked up 13 tackles and forced a fumble for the Browns (4-2), who are tied with the Ravens (4-2) and Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) atop the division. The Steelers defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime on Sunday. Audric Estime rushed for a touchdown five days after the Browns signed him off the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad with starter Quinshon Judkins (knee) ailing. Judkins was eventually ruled out of the contest. Watson was 16-of-26 passing for 164 yards as Cleveland halted a three-game slide against Baltimore. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley started for the Ravens in place of two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson (ankle) for the second straight week. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards and one touchdown. Josh Cuevas caught a scoring pass for Baltimore and Derrick Henry rushed for 58 yards on 17 carries but lost a key fumble. Cleveland trailed 10-0 at halftime before holding the ball for the first 7:12 of the third quarter and getting on the board when Szmyt booted a 48-yard field goal. Baltimore still led by seven when Tyler Loop was wide left on a 49-yard field-goal attempt with 14:13 left in the game. Less than two minutes later, the Ravens had the ball again and Henry was forced to fumble by Schwesinger. Tyson Campbell recovered the ball at the Ravens 35 with 12:36 left in the contest. Seven plays later, Estime scored on a 2-yard run to tie it 10-10 with 8:33 remaining. Cleveland had a chance to take the lead later in the quarter but Szmyt narrowly missed wide left from 48 yards with 3:40 remaining. That ended a streak of 25 straight makes for Szmyt dating to last season. The Ravens opened the game with an 11-play, 66-yard drive that featured Henry runs of 11 and 17 yards. The touchdown came when Cuevas was wide open in the middle of the end zone for a 2-yard reception from Huntley with 8:11 left in the opening quarter. Baltimore increased its lead to 10 when Loop connected on a 34-yard field goal with 4:37 remaining in the opening period. The Browns had just 46 yards and three first downs in the first half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eagles lose edge Nolan Smith to concussion
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Nolan Smith sustained a concussion in the first half of the team's 25-14 home loss against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Nolan Smith sustained a concussion in the first half of the team's 25-14 home loss against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Smith, 25, was rushing the passer with 12:45 left in the second quarter when he was chip-blocked by Carolina running back Chuba Hubbard. Smith fell to the ground and was checked for a concussion in the aftermath of the play. He did not return to the game. The Eagles (2-4) have dealt with a large number of key injuries this season. They entered the Carolina game missing quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley, among others. Smith recorded a first-half sack to bring his season total to three. That matches the 2025 total for the 2023 Eagles first-round draft pick. He now has 13.5 sacks for his career. He has three total tackles in the game and one quarterback hit. --Field Level Media

item.title: Falcons rookie LB Kendal Daniels carted off after tackle vs. Bears
item.description: Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher following a lengthy delay in the third quarter of Sunday's 31-23 home loss to the Chicago Bears.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher following a lengthy delay in the third quarter of Sunday's 31-23 home loss to the Chicago Bears. According to the Falcons, Daniels was conscious and had full movement of all extremities. He was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta for further evaluation. Daniels, 23, stumbled into a low tackle on Chicago tight end Colston Loveland, his facemask colliding with Loveland's knee. Daniels then rolled over while putting his face toward the turf. He remained motionless for several minutes as medical personnel attended to him. "So far the reports are good," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said after the game. "He did have movement in his extremities out there on the field. I thought the medical staff did an outstanding job of getting him safely off the field. So all reports so far are good and we'll continue to pray that they remain good." Daniels, a fourth-round draft pick last April out of Oklahoma, has started on defense in each of his first six NFL games. He entered Sunday with one sack among his 22 tackles and had seven tackles against the Bears before departing. --Field Level Media

item.title: Anthropic to commit 5% stake to new 'public benefit fund'
item.description: AI lab Anthropic, the developer of Claude, said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund so it has increased flexibility and scale to make donations for the "public good."
item.dc:creator: Abu Sultan
item.content:encoded: AI lab Anthropic, the developer of Claude, said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund so it has increased flexibility and scale to make donations for the "public good." The proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2% of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50% increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed. The move comes at a time when Anthropic is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a [USN:L6N45L0UH TEXT:"public benefit corporation"], a legal structure that requires management to consider certain broader interests as well as turning a profit for investors. The company, which has positioned itself as a safety-first AI lab, has said AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" and devoted roughly 80 pages of the 261-page main body of its prospectus to laying out risk factors. Anthropic said in its blog post its Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI’s impact on the labor market. Elon Musk, who runs Anthropic rival xAI, on X said he recommended "giving the shares directly to the public." Anthropic cited the potential impact of AI on workers as one area of focus for the new fund, building on a previously announced $200 million commitment to study and address labor-market disruption. Global companies have [USN:L6N42P0Q1 TEXT:"cut"] thousands of jobs after investing heavily in AI, with many, primarily tech firms, pointing to higher efficiencies from the technology's rapid adoption. IMF research [USN:L1N45Z05I TEXT:"shows"] that some 40% of jobs will be either augmented, downgraded or eliminated by AI, with the number as high as 60% in advanced economies, Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said last week. NOT FOR POLITICAL GIVING The AI giant said none of the equity held by its fund would be used for lobbying or political giving in the United States or abroad. US [USN:L6N43N198 TEXT:"policymakers"] are weighing greater oversight of artificial intelligence and AI companies are stepping up efforts to shape how the technology is regulated. Combined with its co-founders' pledge to donate 80% of their equity and an employee donation matching program, roughly 20% of Anthropic's shares will be dedicated to public purposes, excluding any additional shares added later. Anthropic said it would say more in the coming months on the fund's governance, structure and the valuation thresholds that could expand its ownership stake. It also plans to publish a public-benefit report detailing progress toward its mission.

item.title: Trump says Washington golf course renovation to start in November, despite judge's order
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification. The renovation work, which Trump earlier this year had said [USN:L1N43005N TEXT:"would begin in September"], has become the subject of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns. Trump wrote in a Sunday morning post on Truth Social that work on the East Potomac Golf Links would begin on November 15 and that it would reopen in about 15 months. Trump later posted that the Interior Department, which oversees the golf course, "is very excited" about the latest renovation plans. The renovation is among [USN:L6N41H110 TEXT:"a number of projects"] Trump is pursuing to reshape the White House and other Washington landmarks. US District Judge Ana Reyes ruled earlier this year that the government must give notice before any substantive construction work on the golf course could proceed, and last week [USN:L1N45Y0L4 TEXT:"issued an order"] halting the removal of trees at the site, which she called "inexcusable." After the president's posts appeared on Truth Social, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to explain whether it maintained its position argued last week that there is "no final agency action" regarding the course, and that at most, "the President has given preliminary thought" to the renovations. Responding to the judge's order, Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward wrote in a filing that any redesign of the golf course is not an "agency action." "Just as a decision to redesign all the art exhibits in a Smithsonian Museum would not be agency action, neither would a decision to redesign a golf course, or to trim trees, replace fences, expand the fairways, or mow the lawn," Woodward wrote. The DC Preservation League brought a lawsuit in February to halt the administration's takeover of the golf course, alleging that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American history." In an October 9 court filing, the Trump administration had asked Reyes to dismiss the litigation, saying it was premature because the "proposed project remains at an early and conceptual stage." The following day, however, the government removed about 500 trees from the site, which it said would improve safety at the park and restore its original design, and was part of a 2019 plan that predates Trump's ambitions for the course. Reyes ordered a halt to the removals. On Friday, the government filed a motion to disqualify Reyes and move the case to another district judge, saying her actions had shown "deep-seated and unequivocal antipathy toward the Trump Administration," according to court records.

item.title: Brazil's Bolsonaro, Lula spar in first debate as personal attacks fly
item.description: Brazil's Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva traded barbs in their first face-to-face presidential debate on Sunday in a contentious back-and-forth just one week before the election's runoff.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle
item.content:encoded: Brazil's Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva traded barbs in their first face-to-face presidential debate on Sunday in a contentious back-and-forth just one week before the election's runoff. Polls before the debate suggested Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, would enter the October 25 vote as the favorite after finishing nearly two points ahead of Lula in the [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"election's first round"] earlier this month. But surveys have also shown a [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"narrowing race"], and Lula has expressed confidence he can be the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy in the 1980s to finish second in the first round and go on to win the election. The debate, which allowed the candidates to tensely move about the stage and interact with each other with limited moderation from the host, turned quickly into a heated exchange of corruption accusations and personal attacks. Lula pressed Bolsonaro on [USN:L1N4530F5 TEXT:"alleged links to"] jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, and Bolsonaro questioned Lula about [USN:L1N43X02G TEXT:"accusations involving his son"] and a pension fraud scandal. "Lying is the Bolsonaro family’s strong suit," Lula said, while Bolsonaro said Lula has a "very clear problem in your DNA" and is "always tainted by corruption." Sunday's debate was the first between Lula and Senator Bolsonaro after the candidates both declined previous opportunities. A second debate is scheduled for October 23 just ahead of the runoff. Lula told reporters before the debate that he hoped to win over the 33 million voters who stayed home in the election's first round, equal to about one in five eligible voters. TENSE EXCHANGES The debate's format at times fueled tense exchanges and vocal frustration from the audience. A confident Bolsonaro gestured and paced several times behind Lula when it was the president's turn to speak, a move that moderators said was within the rules but that drew complaints from Lula's team. "Bolsonaro had a slight advantage overall, more so based on posture than on content, because Lula was uncomfortable and nervous throughout the entire debate," said Lucas de Aragao, a partner at Brasilia-based consultancy Arko Advice. At one point, Lula refused to stand near Bolsonaro, calling him a "militiaman," alluding to allegations of the senator's ties to Rio de Janeiro paramilitary groups. Bolsonaro, in turn, quipped that it was good he had left his wallet behind, an apparent jab at Lula’s 2017 corruption conviction that was later annulled. The candidates largely repeated campaign promises on policy. Bolsonaro, for example, pledged to designate Brazil’s major gangs and militias as narco-terrorist organizations and build more than half a million prison spaces. Lula defended his economic record, arguing that growth comes from putting money “in the hands of many” rather than a few, and pointed to above-inflation minimum wage increases during his presidency as a sign of his commitment. The candidates clashed over high food prices, which have weighed on Lula's support even with inflation falling and unemployment hitting a record low. "Is food more expensive or cheaper? How long has it been since you put a piece of meat in your freezer?” asked Bolsonaro. The candidates also accused each other of betraying national sovereignty. Lula accused the Bolsonaros of lobbying the US to impose tariffs on Brazil and of hoping Brazil would suffer. "It’s notable to the Brazilian people that the Bolsonaro family is subordinate to American interests," Lula said. Bolsonaro rejected Lula's claims and said that under Lula, Brazil was “subordinate to globalists and terrorists.” BITTER POLITICS Earlier on Sunday, Bolsonaro supporters filled Sao Paulo’s Paulista Avenue, while Lula supporters packed the plaza at the heart of Brasilia’s government district, and students in Rio de Janeiro marched against Bolsonaro. The demonstrations laid bare some of the grievances behind the polarization that has gridlocked Brazilian politics for nearly a decade. Many Bolsonaro supporters believe Lula should be imprisoned over corruption scandals that engulfed his Workers’ Party. Many Lula supporters, meanwhile, say former President Bolsonaro’s conviction for a coup attempt was justified. In Sao Paulo, demonstrators hoisted a giant inflatable of Lula in a prison uniform. “I don’t like bandits. Out with Lula!” said protester Vera de Sousa. In Brasilia, rally-goers chanted “Bolsonaro in jail” beside an effigy of the former president with bloodied hands. “We need the current government to remain in power. If another government comes in, we’re - excuse my language - screwed,” said Lula supporter Sonia Maria. Lula spent 580 days in prison in 2018 and 2019 on a corruption conviction that was later annulled over flaws in the investigation and legal proceedings. Former President Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years for plotting a coup after losing his 2022 reelection bid to Lula. He is serving the sentence under house arrest because of health problems. The younger Bolsonaro has called his father’s trial a “farce” and has pledged to seek amnesty for him if elected president.

item.title: Captain of flydubai plane describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked
item.description: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door. Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE attorney general has said was an [USN:L6N45V0UP TEXT:"attempted suicide attack"] by the co-pilot who intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport. Speaking in an interview with The National newspaper from a hospital bed in Abu Dhabi, his head and left arm bandaged, Machchhar said that when the first blow landed, he thought something had gone "horribly wrong the aircraft structure", before quickly realising he was being attacked and things had "taken a drastic turn". "The next thought was I need to get help in here," he said in the interview published on Saturday. "My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts and I tried to just block the blows as much as I could," he said, pointing to his arm that was wounded as he defended himself. "The blows were coming on the head." "Immediately my hand went to the knob which opens the door and screaming for my colleagues, screaming his name." "I believe that was the first time when I lost my consciousness." The aircraft, flight FZ1073, was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for emergency use. The incident caused the airliner to plunge 16,000 feet (4,900 meters) in 30 seconds before the attacker was overwhelmed and two other pilots who were on board landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The suspect, an Omani national, was transferred to the UAE, flydubai's home country. The plan was inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors say, as a result of their criminal investigation launched on October 1. Machchhar said he heard the cockpit door opening and screaming "between my colleague and the guy". He said the scariest thing he felt was the aircraft nose "steeply going down." "I was not very sure that I'll make it out alive from this. Did I give up? No."

item.title: Strong winds fueled grass fire at Canadian military base that killed four
item.description: Flames that killed four Canadian soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smoldering grass fire that quickly grew in an Alberta base's training area where personnel were carrying out exercises, officials said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Stephenson
item.content:encoded: Flames that killed four Canadian soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smoldering grass fire that quickly grew in an Alberta base's training area where personnel were carrying out exercises, officials said on Sunday. Officials said 39 people were in hospitals as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which Prime Minister Mark Carney described as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on home soil. Winds up to 96 kilometers (60 miles) per hour fed the blaze which began around 4 p.m. MDT (2200 GMT) on Saturday. But they were below 50 km per hour leading up to the fire, Major General Wade Rutland told reporters at a news conference. He described the sudden high winds and resulting spread of the fire as an "uncommon, rapid" event in which the flames advanced 1 km in 30 to 60 seconds. "I’ve certainly never seen anything like it," said Rutland, commander of 1st Canadian Division, which is based in Edmonton, about 210 km west of the military site. Officials identified the dead as Sergeant Morgan Wong, Private Shaun Farrell, Private Aidan Goulding and Private Hayden Lykkemark. "The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honor the victims. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said many of the injured will require "weeks and months" of specialized, intensive medical care. When the fire began, Rutland said, 85 soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, were in "high intensity" combat training using live munitions at the base, which is located in a prairie setting. The soldiers were preparing for deployment to Latvia, where Canadian forces currently have their largest international military operation. Rutland said the incident remains under investigation and declined to speculate on what caused the grass fire. Officials do not believe the region's extensive oil and gas infrastructure had anything to do with the incident, he said. He also ruled out "outside interference." CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country. Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable," Carney said. Twenty-two ground ambulances and eight air ambulances responded to the scene, Smith said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer. Military search and rescue technicians also parachuted into the site, Rutland said. Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange," or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright. The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6,600, is just north of the base. The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.

item.title: US officials visit Palestinian village after settler attacks on diplomats
item.description: While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attack, Benjamin Netanyahu, whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, has been more circumspect.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Steven Scheer
item.content:encoded: US diplomats visited a Christian Palestinian village in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday following attacks by militant Israeli settlers on [USN:L1N46305Z TEXT:"European diplomats"] and an [USN:L1N4620BI TEXT:"American photojournalist"] in the previous two days. Riley Barnes, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labor, Brian Burch, US ambassador to the Holy See, and a number of other diplomats visited the Latin Convent church and were expected to meet with members of the Christian community in Taybeh. Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor and Palestinian civilians, had been attacked near Taybeh on Saturday by masked Israeli settlers. The previous day, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was taken to hospital after being assaulted while covering a Palestinian olive harvest near another West Bank village. The diplomats' visit coincided with US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N46403J TEXT:"endorsing"] his ally, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for Israel's parliamentary election on October 27. Meanwhile, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee attended a settler conference in the West Bank on Sunday. Huckabee, an evangelical Christian and longtime supporter of Israel, earlier wrote on X calling for "those who attacked" the Washington Post photojournalist, a US citizen, to be jailed. NETANYAHU CIRCUMSPECT ON SETTLER VIOLENCE Trump has expressed his opposition to Israeli annexation of the West Bank, but his administration has put little [USN:L6N45G09W TEXT:"pressure on Netanyahu's"] right-wing, pro-settler government to change its policy. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied. While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military both blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attack on the diplomats, Netanyahu, whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, has been more circumspect. He has said the diplomats entered a "sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination" with the Israeli military, and that the facts of the attack on Levine are "unclear". France urged Israeli authorities to arrest Saturday's attackers and to end criminal violence in the West Bank, but by Sunday there was no announcement from Israeli authorities of any arrests in either of the two latest incidents. The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinians. Settler attacks on the Palestinians are surging, with at least 170 since September 27, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli human rights group. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. Yet prosecutions of Israeli settlers are rare. On Sunday, Reuters saw a group of at least 10 settlers, masked and dressed in black, hurling rocks at Palestinians and activists harvesting olives near the Palestinian West Bank town of Salfit, prompting the farmers to flee. Israeli border police were in the area and shot tear gas towards the hills.

item.title: Arsenal edge Forest with late goal, Man United held by Leeds
item.description: Champions Arsenal needed a late goal from Noni Madueke, their only shot on target, to scrape a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest and remain three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Champions Arsenal needed a late goal from Noni Madueke, their only shot on target, to scrape a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday and remain three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City. Brighton & Hove Albion's Diego Gomez struck a sensational goal from inside his own half in a 5-0 rout of Crystal Palace on Sunday to leave his side third in the table with 16 points, five behind leaders Manchester City. Manchester United and bitter rivals Leeds United shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw at Elland Road at the end of a turbulent week for the Red Devils in which defender Lisandro Martinez had publicly challenged the club's hierarchy. Leeds are seventh in the table and Manchester United, who have just one win from seven games, are 13th. Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 for their first league victory of the season to climb to 15th place. Sunderland remained in the drop zone in 19th place. At the City Ground, a frustrated Arsenal finally sealed victory in the 80th minute. Ibrahim Sangare hesitated when he could have cleared the ball, leaving Forest manager Oliver Glasner visibly fuming, and second-half substitute Madueke then danced past Daniel Munoz before hammering a shot that deflected off Jair Cunha and wrong-footed Matz Sels. "We're really happy, we did it all together. We showed grit, determination, and maybe we showed a champion spirit here for that, really pleased," Madueke told Sky Sports. Murillo almost salvaged a point for Forest in injury time when he beat three players before unleashing a shot that sailed agonisingly wide. The defeat left Forest, who have yet to win or even score at the City Ground this season, in the drop zone in 18th place with five points. At the Amex, Brighton got on the scoresheet in the fourth minute through a Jaydee Canvot own goal, before Gomez struck a goal of the season contender three minutes later, robbing Adam Wharton of the ball near the halfway line before taking a touch and firing the ball over keeper Walter Benitez and into the net. "When I got the ball I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead," Gomez told Sky Sports. "When I scored I didn't know where to run or what to do. I was very happy with the goal." Yasin Ayari padded Brighton's lead three minutes later, before Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood completed the rout after the break. Kostoulas scored just after halftime when Ayari's shot deflected into the Greece international's path, and Hinshelwood struck in the 84th when Luka Vuskovic's header was scooped off the line by Benitez and he fired home the rebound. MBEUMO GRABS OPENING GOAL Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the 35th minute after missing a couple of chances. Mbeumo held off James Justin before tapping in a Youri Tielemans cross from six yards out. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised in the 51st minute, chesting down the ball from a corner before poking home. "We are slightly disappointed it is just a point," Leeds boss Daniel Farke told Sky. "Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. "We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester United." Manchester defender Martinez retained his place in Michael Carrick's starting lineup despite criticising United's hierarchy following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, questioning the club’s summer investment and singling out director of football Jason Wilcox before later apologising. Bournemouth punished a shaky Sunderland start to take the lead after just six minutes, when Lewis Cook lofted a long ball forward that Evanilson ran on to and squared for Marcus Tavernier to head home from close range. Evanilson scored himself in the 48th minute when the Brazilian rounded goalkeeper Robin Roefs before slotting home left-footed.

item.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in close Israeli election
item.description: The endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the October 27 national election.
item.dc:creator: Doina Chiacu, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election. Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minister" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilizing regional economies. "Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure — But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today." In his message, addressed to "the Great People of Israel," Trump added, "Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel." The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the October 27 national election, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran. Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote. It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era. Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to his "dear friend Donald" on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!" Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras. ENDORSEMENT MIGHT HELP, CAN'T HURT Trump's relationship with Netanyahu has been close but also fractious, with the president at times publicly and privately criticizing Israel's longest-serving prime minister. The war that the US and Israel launched against Iran is unpopular with Americans, who vote November 3 in congressional elections, while support for Israel among Americans has also decreased over the Iran war and Israel's conduct in the three-year war in Gaza that Trump has promised to end. Both leaders on Sunday mentioned finishing the job in Iran. Tamar Hermann, a senior research fellow at the non-partisan Israel Democracy Institute in Jerusalem, said Trump's late endorsement could help win back wavering Netanyahu voters but was unlikely to draw widespread support. Most Israelis, even those who are critical of Netanyahu and his government, were largely in favor of the Iran war. In an election this close, "it couldn't hurt him, and it might help," said analyst Aaron David Miller of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Washington. Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, although the opposition may also struggle to form a government, opinion polls show. That could lead to Netanyahu serving as a caretaker prime minister while another election is held. The US president passed up earlier opportunities to endorse Netanyahu, perhaps because he wanted to see what leverage he could exercise on issues like Gaza or Lebanon, said Miller. In the end, he said, Trump sided with a leader he sees as strong and unfairly persecuted. "However angry Trump may be at Netanyahu for pushing this Iran war, this in the end was a Trump decision," Miller added. A Trump decision not to endorse Netanyahu would have raised "legitimate questions about whether or not the whole Iran venture was in fact something Trump should have done," he said.

item.title: Huracán Trudy se debilita frente a costa del Pacífico mexicano, comienzan labores de limpieza
item.description: El huracán Trudy se debilitaba el domingo frente a la costa del Pacífico mexicano mientras se alejaba del continente, informaron autoridades meteorológicas de México y Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se debilitaba el domingo frente a la costa del Pacífico mexicano mientras se alejaba del continente, informaron autoridades meteorológicas de México y Estados Unidos. El Centro Nacional de Huracanes estadounidense (NHC, por sus siglas en inglés) dijo en su reporte más reciente que Trudy se ubicaba a unos 290 kilómetros al oeste-noroeste de Manzanillo, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 155 kilómetros por hora (km/h), y avanzaba hacia el noroeste a 9 km/h. Se esperaba que el centro de Trudy se alejara aún más de la costa mexicana antes de pasar cerca del sur de Baja California Sur entre el lunes y el martes. El Gobierno de México levantó todas las alertas por huracán y tormenta tropical a lo largo de la costa del Pacífico y en el archipiélago de las Islas Marías. Sin embargo, las autoridades recomendaron mantener vigilancia preventiva en el suroeste y centro-oeste del país, así como en Baja California Sur. Por otra parte, las autoridades advirtieron sobre condiciones meteorológicas severas asociadas con el frente frío número 2 en el sur y sureste del país. La Coordinación Nacional de Protección Civil dijo que se esperaba que el sistema permaneciera estacionario sobre el sur del estado Veracruz, con potencial de provocar lluvias extraordinarias y torrenciales. Añadió que mantendría una estrecha vigilancia sobre los niveles de ríos y embalses de ese estado además de Tabasco, Chiapas y Oaxaca. Los fuertes vientos del norte y oleaje de hasta seis metros ya habían provocado inundaciones en zonas costeras y cierres de carreteras en algunas zonas de Tabasco. En Veracruz, más de 1,500 viviendas resultaron afectadas por inundaciones, mientras las autoridades realizaban labores de limpieza y recuperación a medida que descendían gradualmente los niveles del agua. En las últimas semanas, la costa del Pacífico mexicano ha sido afectada por los huracanes [USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:"Polo y Simon"], así como por la tormenta Rachel. Las inundaciones dejaron al menos ocho muertos en la ciudad costera de Ensenada, en el estado de Baja California.

item.title: Romanian F-16 fighter jets shoot down two drones over Romanian territorial waters
item.description: Romanian F-16 fighter jets shot down two drones over the country's territorial waters on Saturday, the defence ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Romanian F-16 fighter jets shot down two drones over the country's territorial waters on Saturday, the defence ministry said. Defence Minister Radu Miruta said on Sunday the drones were likely latest generation Russian drones, flying at speeds similar to fighter jets. "The ones from last night were flying at 450 km/h, which leads us to think they were Russian-made Geran-4 drones with a turboprop engine," Miruta said. "This is the first time we've shot down drones like these." The drones were [USN:L8N4610EC TEXT:"brought down"] days after two chemical tankers were hit by drones near Romania's Black Sea coast, the latest in a series of attacks highlighting risks to commercial shipping on NATO's eastern flank. Both vessels were anchored near the Sulina Canal, which links the Danube River to the Black Sea and is an export route for Ukraine. NATO member Romania shares a 614-km (381-mile) border with Ukraine, much of it along the Danube, and has repeatedly reported Russian drone incursions into its airspace since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Romania started [USN:L8N43Q0KW TEXT:"shooting down drones"] that enter its space earlier this year. The defence ministry said the two drones entered Romanian waters in the Black Sea on Saturday at 1459 GMT and 1501 GMT, respectively. "NATO is ready and able to react to any potential threat, 24/7, to safeguard our territory and protect our people," a NATO official told Reuters. Romania's Foreign Minister Oana Toiu said the North Atlantic Council will have a meeting on Tuesday to discuss Black Sea defence and deterrence. The two tankers struck earlier this week were hit by Russian drones, a NATO military source told Reuters. Romanian officials are still [USN:L8N4620JP TEXT:"searching"] for seven missing crew members. At least five other cargo ships have been hit near the coasts of Romania and neighbouring Bulgaria in the past two weeks, with 23 sailors reported dead or missing. Most of those incidents occurred outside NATO territorial waters. In Moldova, on Romania's northeast border, officials said a new drone had crashed in a northern district, near the border with Ukraine. Officials said there were no casualties or damage and specialists were trying to determine the drone's origin. Five drones identified as Russian [USN:L1N46210E TEXT:"fell on Moldovan territory"] in a little more than 17 hours on Thursday and Friday, prompting the foreign ministry to issue a statement denouncing Russian actions.

item.title: US resumes intelligence-sharing with Ukraine after pause, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Speaking to NBC's Meet the Press, Zelenskiy said intelligence-sharing was interrupted and later "de-blocked."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States has resumed providing Ukraine critical intelligence to help it defend against Russian missile strikes, after a brief pause, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said in comments published on Sunday. Ukraine has relied on US intelligence to spot the fast-moving ballistic missiles that Russia has fired in waves at its cities. US President Donald Trump had [USN:L1N45Z16F TEXT:"said earlier this week"] that Washington was still sharing intelligence, although Ukrainian officials said some Russian strikes had occurred without warning. Speaking to NBC's Meet the Press, Zelenskiy said intelligence-sharing had been interrupted but later "de-blocked." "We are very thankful for this," he said. "Now it works." But Zelenskiy said other US actions, such as signing a deal to import Russian diesel and [USN:L6N464042 TEXT:"waiving sanctions on Russia"] that had been slated to take effect this week, will hurt Ukraine. "If the United States will officially take the side of Russia, of course if these two countries will be together, of course we will not prevail and we will not be able to stand," he said. Over the past week, a [USN:L6N46303A TEXT:"widening rift"] between Trump and Zelenskiy has sparked concerns that their tumultuous relationship could lead to even worse outcomes for Kyiv. Zelenskiy told NBC that he hopes Trump will remain an ally of Ukraine. "We want to trust him, and I hope that he will change his decisions," Zelenskiy said. "Because I think that it's all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help United States." In a Truth Social post on Sunday afternoon, Trump wrote that his decision-making was aimed at avoiding anything "that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table." Ukraine gets US help that Russia does not receive, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told NBC, citing intelligence-sharing and the provision of US munitions to other countries for resale to Ukraine. But Bessent, speaking with "Meet the Press" after it aired Zelenskiy's interview, did not directly answer when asked multiple times whether the United States views Ukraine as an ally. "Zelenskiy presents a false binary this morning that Ukraine must win," Bessent said. "The war must end, and that will be with some kind of a negotiated settlement."

item.title: Hurricane Trudy weakens off Mexico's Pacific coast as cleanup effort begins
item.description: Hurricane Trudy weakened slightly off Mexico's Pacific coast on Sunday and was expected to begin rapidly losing strength later in the day as it moved away from the mainland, forecasters said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Trudy weakened slightly off Mexico's Pacific coast on Sunday and was expected to begin rapidly losing strength later in the day as it moved away from the mainland, forecasters said. The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) said Trudy was located about 180 miles (290 km) west-northwest of Manzanillo, with maximum sustained winds of 100 mph (155 kph), down from 105 mph earlier in the day, moving northwest at 6 mph (9 kph). Trudy's center is expected to move farther away from Mexico's Pacific coast before passing south of Baja California Sur on Monday and Tuesday. Mexico's government, meanwhile, discontinued all hurricane and tropical storm warnings along the Pacific coast and for the Islas Marias archipelago, but authorities said locals in southwestern and west-central Mexico, as well as Baja California Sur, should continue to monitor the storm. Separately, Mexican authorities warned of severe weather linked to Cold Front No. 2 in the country's south and southeast. The National Civil Protection Coordination said the system was expected to stall over southern Veracruz, bringing extraordinary and torrential rainfall. In Veracruz, more than 1,500 homes were affected by floodwaters, while federal, state and municipal authorities were carrying out cleanup and recovery operations as water levels gradually receded. Civil protection authorities also said they were closely monitoring river and reservoir levels in Veracruz, Tabasco, Chiapas and Oaxaca, while strong northerly winds and waves of up to 6 meters (20 feet) had already caused coastal flooding and road closures in parts of Tabasco.

item.title: IMF/World Bank meetings leave developing countries with more questions than answers
item.description: Last week's meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank yielded no new answers for the developing world to the questions posed by a spreading Middle East war, continuing war in Ukraine, rising debt payments and a potential AI bubble.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, David Lawder
item.content:encoded: Last week's meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank yielded no new answers for the developing world to the questions posed by a spreading Middle East war, continuing war in Ukraine, rising debt payments and a potential AI bubble. Not for the first time, [USN:L1N46302K TEXT:"lower-income countries"] are being rocked by the spillover from the actions of wealthier nations: rising debt service costs, higher inflation and the risk of falling ever further behind economically thanks to the AI boom. What they got was the stock advice the global lenders always dish out: to shrink fiscal deficits and accelerate economic reforms to attract more private sector investment. Kristalina Georgieva, the first IMF chief from a developing nation - Bulgaria - said advanced economies were in fact the worst offenders on budget imbalances. She noted that developing countries' debt levels had actually fallen in recent years, only for surging bond yields elsewhere to drive up their borrowing costs. Average debt service payments there had more than doubled from a decade ago to 14% of government revenue, crowding out education, healthcare and other critical areas, she said. ADVANCED ECONOMIES FOCUSED ON THEIR OWN PROBLEMS At a panel on Saturday, Georgieva said many issues remained unresolved, especially around AI: "We are in a place where we have many more questions than we have answers. And my alert to everybody is: Do not fall for the guys that pretend they have the answers. They are tricking you." Josh Lipsky, vice president of international economics at the Atlantic Council think tank, said the meetings had flunked their opportunity to come up with guidance or ways to help. "It's hard to talk about the developing world when the advanced economies don't have their act together and are at risk of a fiscal crisis," he said. "And that's on top of political situations in many of these countries that makes development aid not a priority at the moment." Mauricio Cardenas, Colombia's former finance minister and now a research scholar at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs in New York, said many policymakers were left with a deep sense that "something really bad could happen" but no real roadmap to navigate the future. "The IMF and World Bank are not particularly well prepared for this new phase. They understand that something is going on, they bring in experts on AI," he said. "But in the end, there's no kind of specific, concrete advice on how to be prepared for something where you don't really understand how it's going to unfold." The geopolitical tensions that have roiled both institutions since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 - complicating concerted action - were also evident in Bangkok when nearly half the delegates at an [USN:L1N46301V TEXT:"IMF steering committee"] walked out when Russia's finance minister spoke. Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport delayed the arrival of the head of that committee, Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan, who had to travel overland to Qatar to catch a flight. And Bangkok itself was a stark reminder of the challenges facing developing countries, still partly under water after floods in September that caused almost $200 million in damage to Thailand's industrial sector. RISING INEQUALITY COULD RAISE COSTS IN LONG TERM Kate Pickett, a professor at the University of York, urged policymakers to focus on more inclusive growth rather than forcing developing countries into tough structural reforms. "If inequality increases, if poverty deepens, that will increase their costs in the long term," she said. "It's not enough to describe an economy as resilient. It's only resilient for the rich and the privileged.” Ayhan Kose, deputy chief economist at the World Bank, said the global economy had weathered its biggest energy shock - from the US-Israeli war on Iran - better than expected. But while a global recession had been avoided, he said growth outlooks in both developing and advanced economies were worse than before. Growth had already fallen off in half of advanced economies, while in developing countries as a whole, it had slowed significantly to around 3.6% from 4.4%. “People are really worried because resilience today is not a guarantee for resilience tomorrow," he said. "Now they are worried about what will be the next shock, because every six months, if not every three months, there is a new shock." While no specific initiatives were announced, he said the World Bank remained focused on helping developing countries prepare for advancements in AI, in part by mobilising more private capital, now at triple the levels of 2022. Yet it, too, has to contend with sharp drops in official development aid and persistent challenges in attracting foreign investment to developing countries. “The reality on the ground is the reality on the ground,” he said.

item.title: Iran urges US to accept proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's offer to the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days is still on the table, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told Iranian media outlets on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran's offer to the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days is still on the table, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told Iranian media outlets on Sunday. Iran presented its proposal in mid-September after an [USN:L1N42P0Q6 TEXT:"interim ceasefire"] collapsed. Tehran later acknowledged receiving a US response but [USN:L1N45X04L TEXT:"Iran’s security chief"] said last week negotiations have stalled because Washington failed to address all [USN:L1N45Q01J TEXT:"seven conditions"] for reopening the strait. "Our situation is clear and based on the seven-days proposal presented to the US. They shared comments which we are reviewing, but our proposal is still on the table and if there is any honesty on the US part, which there isn't, the way to reopening the Strait of Hormuz is obvious," Araqchi said while in Baghdad for a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation. Iran's conditions include, among other demands, the lifting of the US blockade on its ports, the lifting of US sanctions on its oil exports as well as ending hostilities on all regional fronts. If Washington accepts Tehran's conditions, the strait could reopen within six days, with talks resuming the following day, Araqchi said. A central point of disagreement has been Washington’s insistence on addressing Iran's [USN:L1N45T0JD TEXT:"nuclear programme"] from the outset. US Vice President JD Vance said earlier this month that Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries' eight-month war. Tehran says negotiations should initially focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which before the war carried about a fifth of the global trade in oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG), and restoring security in the waterway.

item.title: Accenture looks to sell Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion, FT reports
item.description: IT consulting firm Accenture is looking to sell its Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: IT consulting firm Accenture (ACN.N) is looking to sell its Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Accenture has hired JPMorgan (JPM.N) to work on a strategic review of the China business after receiving unsolicited interest in the unit over the past year, the report added. Accenture and JPMorgan did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment outside regular business hours. The sale process is likely to draw interest from private equity groups and a small cluster of strategic buyers, the report said. Accenture may opt to retain a significant minority stake in the business, the report added. Accenture’s Greater China operations include Taiwan, Hong Kong and mainland China, according to its website. The consultancy firm recently forecast full-year 2027 revenue growth between 3% and 6%, above analysts' estimates.

item.title: Pope Leo pledges gradual return to duties in first event since cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo pledged on Sunday to slowly resume his usual activities as the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics as he greeted crowds in St. Peter's Square during his first public event since undergoing surgery for lung cancer five days ago.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo pledged on Sunday to slowly resume his usual activities as the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics as he greeted crowds in St. Peter's Square during his first public event since undergoing surgery for lung cancer five days ago. The 71-year-old pontiff had an [USN:S8N42Y05U TEXT:"operation"] on Tuesday to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, [USN:L8N4600P9 TEXT:"fuelling speculation"] about how his illness might change his 17-month papacy. Smiling from a window of the Vatican's Apostolic Palace as he spoke to pilgrims below in a firm, clear voice on Sunday, the first US pope thanked people across the world for their prayers and said he would now begin to resume his normal schedule. "Having overcome this delicate phase... I will now gradually resume my activities, always with the help of God and your prayers," Leo said. The pope, who was discharged from Rome's Gemelli hospital on Saturday, came to the window in the palace unaided and held his weekly midday appointment as usual. He also urged pilgrims waiting below under cloudy skies to set aside any selfish ambitions and serve God "without compromise". NUN CRIES AS LEO MAKES APPEARANCE Leo has been diagnosed with [USN:L8N46006S TEXT:"lung adenocarcinoma"], the most common form of lung cancer. The diagnosis, for the youngest pope in decades, who was elected only in May 2025, caused shock. His doctors discharged him on Saturday after blood tests and chest imaging that day showed him well enough to return home. They said he was able to perform normal daily activities independently. Crowds in St. Peter's Square, numbering about 15,000 according to the Vatican, shouted and clapped loudly as Leo first appeared at the window on Sunday. One Catholic nun knelt and cried, holding her hand over her face. A few steps away, a group of other nuns held aloft a sign reading, "Best wishes, Holy Father. We love you and we are praying for you". POPE'S CALENDAR IN FLUX Leo usually keeps a busy schedule, but the Vatican has cancelled his other public events until at least Wednesday, when he is due to hold a weekly general audience in St. Peter's Square. It has not said whether he will hold that audience. The pope is also planning to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17, in one of the most intense trips arranged for a Catholic leader [USN:L8N45D0VL TEXT:"in decades"]. Dr. Stefano Margaritora, the pope's lead surgeon, said on Saturday that Leo could be fully recovered in time for that trip. Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican's secretary of state, has however expressed scepticism. He told journalists on Friday the pope may need to adjust the pace of his schedule going forward "according to the condition of his health".

item.title: Roy Cooper's North Carolina playbook is working. Can other Democrats copy it?
item.description: North Carolina hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate in nearly 20 years, but former Governor Roy Cooper, who hasn't lost an election in four decades, has built a double-digit lead over Republican Michael Whatley.
item.dc:creator: Yasmeen Abutaleb
item.content:encoded: North Carolina hasn’t elected a Democrat to the US Senate in nearly 20 years, but former Governor Roy Cooper has built a double-digit lead over Republican Michael Whatley by relentlessly focusing on affordability and a blunt promise to “make stuff cost less.” At campaign stops, Cooper, 69, points to his six-year fight to expand Medicaid through a Republican-controlled legislature as evidence he can work across party lines, while attacking Trump-backed healthcare cuts that he says are hitting North Carolinians hard. “People should not have to make a choice between going to a doctor and putting food on the table,” Cooper said at a September 26 rally in Raleigh, North Carolina. “This 'Big Beautiful Bill' that gave tax cuts to billionaires has now driven healthcare premiums up more than double for people.” The White House says the bill cuts taxes, protects Medicaid for eligible Americans and curbs fraud and abuse. Cooper's message appears to be working: His lead stood at 14 points in an October SurveyUSA poll. The top super PAC for Senate Republicans has paused TV advertising in North Carolina less than three weeks before the election and begun shifting campaign dollars to defend seats in states that include Iowa and Kansas. President Donald Trump will rally in the state on Tuesday for Whatley, a former Republican National Committee chair who has never held elected office. The question for Democrats is whether Cooper's playbook can help them win Republican and independent voters elsewhere, or whether his success is unique to a popular former governor who has never lost an election in four decades of public service. While some Democrats in heavily Democratic states have embraced Medicare for All, which would provide government-run health insurance for all Americans, Cooper has focused on expanding existing coverage and lowering costs. He points to his fight to expand Medicaid, the government health insurance program for low-income Americans, and campaigns on prescription drug and insurance costs. 'OUR STAR ATHLETE AND NO ONE'S PAYING ANY ATTENTION' “It’s like he’s our star athlete and no one’s paying any attention,” said Neera Tanden, president of the Center for American Progress, a Democratic-aligned think tank, and former White House adviser to President Joe Biden. “The strength of Roy Cooper’s campaign is that he’s able to attract Democrats and independents, but also even some Republicans because he’s focused on cost, but he also has a record.” Paul Shumaker, a longtime Republican strategist in North Carolina, attributes Cooper’s success to the fact he was already well-known and that Whatley failed to distinguish himself from Trump. “Roy Cooper came to the US Senate race with a known brand that has been trusted by a majority of North Carolina voters election after election,” Shumaker said. “Republicans are suffering from a lack of trust on the economy right now and Whatley has failed to reestablish that trust.” Cooper declined an interview request for this story. The Whatley campaign did not respond to a request for comment, but on Sunday he predicted victory during an interview with Fox News. Trump's upcoming visit to North Carolina and an expected rally with Vice President JD Vance will energize Republican voters, Whatley told Fox News' "Sunday Briefing." "Our election is going to come down to turnout and we're in a state that President Trump won three straight times," Whatley said. WINNING OVER INDEPENDENTS North Carolina’s electorate is unusually independent: 40% of registered voters are unaffiliated with either party, compared with 30% each for Republicans and Democrats. Republicans, however, have dominated the state legislature for more than a decade and redrawn districts to strengthen their grip. Like other Republican candidates, Whatley must contend with Trump’s record-low approval rating, which now hovers at 32%, according to an October [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"]. That poll also showed registered voters preferring Democrats over Republicans nationally by 44% to 37%. Among independents, Democrats led 37% to 21%, with 28% of independent voters still undecided. Republicans hold a 53-47 majority in the US Senate, where Democrats must net four seats in the November 3 midterm elections to control the chamber — an already difficult task that makes Cooper's North Carolina race especially important. Cooper's signature bipartisan achievement did not come easily. It took him six years to persuade the Republican-controlled state legislature to pass an expansion of Medicaid under Obamacare in 2023, extending health insurance to more than 700,000 state residents, according to state health department data. After passage, he called it “an unnecessarily long and agonizing journey.” Whit Ayres, a Republican pollster, said several moderate Democratic governors in the South could replicate Cooper’s success, including Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear. “The Roy Coopers of the world are not unique,” Ayres said. “The Republicans nominated someone who’s never been elected to any public office at any level anywhere running against a reasonably moderate, popular governor.” RUNNING AGAINST HEALTHCARE CUTS Many of the state’s Medicaid gains are likely to be undone by Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill,” a sweeping tax and budget bill the Republican-led Congress passed last year that cuts about $1 trillion from Medicaid, the largest cut in the program’s history, according to the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office. Cooper has used Trump’s signature domestic legislative achievement to paint the president and Republicans as depriving North Carolinians of healthcare in order to give billionaires more tax cuts. He has also focused on congressional Republicans’ decision to curtail COVID-era Obamacare subsidies last year, causing healthcare premiums on the individual health insurance marketplace to spike and more than 200,000 state residents to drop their coverage, according to health policy research firm KFF. “Roy Cooper has always polled over Republicans,” said Anderson Clayton, chair of the North Carolina Democratic Party. “This will be the average election for Roy Cooper.”

item.title: Microsoft pulls out of UK data center deal with Nscale, Telegraph reports
item.description: Microsoft has pulled out of a data center deal with British cloud provider Nscale, Britain's Telegraph newspaper reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Microsoft (MSFT.O) has pulled out of a data center deal with British cloud provider Nscale, Britain's Telegraph newspaper reported on Sunday. The US tech giant, one of Nscale's two largest customers, recently terminated its agreement for the data center in Loughton, Essex, according to the report. The newspaper did not specify why Microsoft withdrew from the project. Microsoft declined a Reuters request for comment. The Telegraph report said Nscale had faced repeated delays with the project. National power grid officials, it reported, had told Nscale they did not expect a power supply for the data center until the 2030s. "Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term, and this unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts," an Nscale spokesperson told Reuters. "We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK, and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK." Nscale filed for an [USN:L4N45A197 TEXT:"initial public offering"] in the US last month, with Microsoft and Anthropic expected to be its major customers, according to its prospectus. Nscale [USN:L4N45A1JP TEXT:"provides"] infrastructure, including compute, power and data centers, as well as software for training and running AI models. The Nvidia-backed (NVDA.O) AI group, which competes against CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , Nebius (NBIS.O) , Crusoe and Lambda, has grown rapidly since its launch, scaling from $100 million to more than $103 billion in total contracted value in just two-and-a-half years.

item.title: Macron urges calm as France counts cost of worst unrest in years
item.description: The French president appealed for calm a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in years, with thousands arrested and shops looted or damaged after protests over high prices and declining public services.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide, Clotaire Achi, Abdul Saboor
item.content:encoded: President Emmanuel Macron appealed for calm on Sunday, a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in years, with thousands arrested and shops looted or damaged after protests over high prices and declining public services. Fresh clashes broke out in Paris and Marseille, where riot police intervened to prevent attempts to ransack businesses. Nationwide demonstrations had erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops pillaged and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. "Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: What was going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?" Macron said in a televised address to the nation. "Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame." Saturday's unrest laid bare the deep anger at Macron, who leaves office in 2027 after a decade in power that has increasingly become defined by social discontent, a weak economy and ballooning debt. Macron said those protesting peacefully had legitimate grievances and their actions should not be confused with those seeking to wreak havoc. He stopped short of declaring a state of emergency, as demanded by some right-wing politicians, but said the government would act to allow prefects to ban protests if necessary to protect public buildings and local businesses. PARIS PROTESTS 'LIKE A WAR ZONE' The government has blamed the violence on what it said were ultra-left groups, as well as criminals it said had instigated the looting. One protester died on Saturday after suffering a cardiac arrest during [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"demonstrations"] in Paris. Police made 2,400 arrests across France, while nearly 1,000 officers were injured, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. Police again clashed with protesters and fired tear gas at Place de la Republique on Sunday afternoon, and protesters had set fire to piles of bicycles. A Reuters witness said there appeared to be several hundred protesters in the area. A massive clean-up operation took place in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and from Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect. "It's like a war zone here!" exclaimed Dutch entrepreneur Tije De Boer, who was visiting Paris with his children and said the unrest forced him to evacuate his hotel at Place de la Republique. More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities on Saturday, marking the convergence of a month-long [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"student movement"] with broader social discontent against rising living costs and declining public services. SEVERAL HUNDRED SHOPS DAMAGED While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully across France on Saturday, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets, and attacked police vehicles and officers. Far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, frontrunner going into next year's presidential campaign, also called for calm, saying France must not become accustomed to images of the country being battered, abused and ransacked. "Violence is not an opinion. Destruction is not a form of expression. And chaos cannot serve as a project for France," she said in a video address. Hard-left France Unbowed presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon said Macron needed to answer the demands of protesting high-school students. In [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"Limoges"], famed for its porcelain, the collapse of the town hall's clock tower in a fiery blaze revived memories of the 2019 fire that devastated Paris' Notre Dame cathedral. Mayor Guillaume Guerin said not enough officers from the national police had been deployed to his city. "There was a clear, premeditated intention to burn down the town hall, and the people inside feared for their lives," Guerin told Reuters on Sunday. He threatened to resign if the city did not receive the funds needed to repair the town hall. Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support on Sunday for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement. French retailer Carrefour's (CARR.PA) CEO Alexandre Bompard told French broadcaster BFMTV that 50 of the company's shops had been damaged, including 20 that were looted, with losses from the damage running into the tens of millions of euros.
